- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 14-day moving avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 14-day SMA as ceiling.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects downward; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and recent price is falling; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven resilience.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period mean reversion; apply a 3–5 day lag correction: if true outcome drops below 10% of 30-day moving avg, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative and price is near support, model tends to ignore support; add a 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid undershoot.
